⚠️ Customer Risk Analysis

💡 Data-Driven Retention Recommendations

Recommendation #1:

📊 Finding: Month-to-month contracts have the highest churn rate at 42.6%.

👥 Impact: 3853 customers affected.

💡 Action: Offer incentives (e.g., first month free or discounts) to switch to 1-year or 2-year contracts.

✅ Benefit: Increase customer commitment and reduce short-term churn.

Recommendation #2:

📊 Finding: New customers (0-1 yr) have the highest churn rate at 47.4%.

👥 Impact: 2164 customers affected.

💡 Action: Implement targeted onboarding programs and early touchpoints.

✅ Benefit: Improve early retention and user experience.

Recommendation #3:

📊 Finding: Electronic check users have the highest churn rate at 45.1%.

👥 Impact: 2359 customers affected.

💡 Action: Encourage migration to automatic payments (Credit Card/Bank Transfer) via small discounts.

✅ Benefit: Reduce payment friction and involuntary churn.

Recommendation #4:

📊 Finding: Customers without Tech Support churn at a rate of 41.5%.

👥 Impact: 3465 customers affected.

💡 Action: Bundle Tech Support with core internet services or offer a free trial.

✅ Benefit: Increase product stickiness and customer satisfaction.

Recommendation #5:

📊 Finding: Fiber optic customers have the highest churn rate at 41.8%.

👥 Impact: 3090 customers affected.

💡 Action: Investigate Fiber Optic service quality, reliability, and pricing.

✅ Benefit: Address specific service issues and retain high-value customers.

Recommendation #6:

📊 Finding: Churned customers pay on average $74.60, which is higher than retained customers ($61.34).

👥 Impact: All 7021 customers potentially impacted by pricing.

💡 Action: Conduct a pricing review and offer flexible, personalized plans.

✅ Benefit: Prevent customers from leaving due to cost concerns.
